set.per_unit_cap: Maximum City loan is 40% of the total residential development cost of the project's affordable units, with the value of any City land donation counted toward that cap; HOME-assisted units are also limited to HUD Region IX per-unit subsidy limits ($181,488 studio to $359,263 four bedroom as of February 13, 2024). Within the cap, awards are sized by gap underwriting to the minimum City subsidy needed (2024 NC NOFA terms; the Tranche 3 NOFA may revise them). Oakland Housing Authority has indicated up to $8,000,000 in operating, predevelopment or capital assistance for NC NOFA and R2H2 projects with PSH or deeply affordable units (OHA Board action pending).
set.affordability_requirement: 2024 NC NOFA: 100% of City-assisted units restricted to low income households at or below 60% AMI with rents no more than 30% of 60% AMI (and at least 10% below market rents within one mile); threshold of at least 20% of affordable units at rents no more than 30% of 30% AMI reserved for extremely low income households, with points for deeper ELI and homeless or special needs targeting; no more than 15% of unassisted affordable units may be moderate income; 55-year regulatory agreement; loans typically 3% simple interest, 55-year term, repaid from residual receipts. Scoring favors public land, ministerial approvals, readiness for tax credits, emerging developer joint ventures, displacement-risk neighborhoods.

set.typical_award_size: Voter-approved $135,000,000 GO bond (November 2018) for development, rehabilitation and preservation of affordable housing for extremely low through middle income households. The City has completed three of four planned issuances. First issuance about $30,000,000 (2019-20) funded Berkeley Way and 1601 Oxford and a 2019 HTF RFP of about $14,500,000. Completed projects include Jordan Court ($3,500,000), Berkeley Way (over $13,800,000) and The Grinnell ($7,300,000). In progress: BUSD workforce housing ($26,500,000, under construction since June 2025), St Paul Terrace ($12,000,000, under construction since April 2026), 1740 San Pablo ($7,500,000 Measure O). Council reserved $40,000,000 of Measure O for the BART sites: up to $20,000,000 for Ashby BART (still in planning) and $20,000,000 within a $26,500,000 City subsidy for North Berkeley BART. Supportive Housing in People's Park and Ephesian Legacy Court reservations will likely include some Measure O. Measure O cannot fund predevelopment or capitalized operating reserves, which the City covers with U1 or fee revenue.
set.next_deadline: No open Measure O round as of November 9, 2026; remaining proceeds are reserved for pipeline projects (Ashby BART up to $20,000,000, North Berkeley BART, SHiPP, Ephesian Legacy Court). On February 10, 2026 Council extended the SHiPP, Ephesian and North Berkeley BART reservations for 24 months (to about February 2028). Verify unreserved balance with HHCS or the Measure O Bond Oversight Committee.
